title: Palaung language - Wikipedia
text: Palaung or Ta'ang (Burmese: ပလောင်ဘာသာ), also known as De'ang (Chinese: 德昂語; Burmese: တအာင်းဘာသာ), is an Austroasiatic dialect cluster spoken by over half a million people in Burma (Shan State) and neighboring countries.

title: Palaung people - Wikipedia
text: There are three main subgroups of Palaung: the Palé, Shwe and Rumai. [1] The Palé, Riang, Rumai and Shwe peoples are grouped together as the De'ang ethnic nationality. The group also includes the Danau (Danaw) who may no longer have a separate identity from the Palé.

title: Palaungic languages - Wikipedia
text: The Palaungic or Palaung–Wa languages are a group of nearly 30 Austroasiatic languages, with scholars disagreeing on exactly which languages to include in the classification.

text: Rumai Palaung is a stable indigenous language of Myanmar and China. It belongs to the Austro-Asiatic language family. The language is used as a first language by all in the ethnic community. It is not known to be taught in schools.
